text: The renowned master of hidden weapons in the Jianghu, the Tang Clan, has a long-standing tradition. Those who enter the clan must first serve as disciples, and outsiders must perform labor to accumulate merit. Only after a period of time can they hope to gain the favor of their mentors, be accepted into the inner circle, adopt the clan name Tang, and learn the profound martial arts that are not publicly shared. Over a decade ago, the Tang Clan faced a great upheaval, with the previous generation of masters scattered or perished, leaving only the current Sect Leader to uphold the clan. However, despite the Sect Leader's tireless efforts, it was difficult to turn the tide. The Tang Clan's numbers have dwindled, their former glory has faded, and now they are surrounded by formidable enemies, making their situation precarious.

text: The Tang Clan once stood alongside the Nangong and Shangguan families as one of the three great families of Jianghu, yet their ways of conducting affairs were vastly different. The Tang Clan did not adhere to the Nangong's strict family teachings of not accepting outsiders, nor did they share the Shangguan family's ambitious approach of widely recruiting followers. While they did accept disciples, there was a distinction between those who entered the inner circle and those of outside lineage. Outsider disciples had to perform labor and accumulate merit before they could hope to gain the favor of their mentors, convert to the inner circle, and adopt the surname Tang, thus gaining access to the profound secrets of martial arts. This rule was established by the founder and has long since become outdated; however, later generations stubbornly clung to it, leading to their current decline.

The Chinese 唐門醜俠 is a compound title, not a possessive; dropping the apostrophe-s matches the parallel Title Case noun-phrase pattern of the sibling Title/0 row and the GLOSSARY rule that titles are noun phrases. 俠 = Hero in compounds per NOMENCLATURE's wuxia-vocabulary table.
